name: Wet-mesic to mesic prairie (higher ground)
reads_as: a shorter, bluer, more forb-crowded sward than the wet prairie, with lavender bergamot and mass yellow coneflower over vegetative bunchgrass

extent.note: There is no survey of the wet/mesic boundary at the forks and no source distinguishes them here at all. This takes the highest ground in the committed heightfield (1.18 m and up, the inland crest of the West Division, about 3.9 ft above the water, at the top of the terrain spec's +3 to +6 ft range for that division) as the drier community. It is a reading of the terrain, not evidence, and a critic should treat the line as ours.

july.appearance: Blue-green leafy clumps, NO flowering culm — about half the September height.
Tight blue-green vegetative bunches; no fluffy white seed — that is September.

species.note: Dossier [I]: regional mesic-prairie matrix, not named at the forks.

width_provenance.note: WHAT ONE DRAWN PLANT COVERS ON THE GROUND, added for ROADMAP K49(c) so this record's cover_fraction can be read as a count of plants. Reasoned from this dataset's own committed Andropogon gerardii clump, [0.30, 0.60] m in this same record. § ZONE 2 gives Indian grass 0.8-1.1 m in July against big bluestem's 0.9-1.3 m, in one bunchgrass matrix; the clumps are taken as one size class. No source states either width.

july.appearance: Leafy vegetative clumps. The bronze plume is a late-August feature.

species.note: Dossier [I] for this site. Held vegetative by the dossier's global phenology rule 1, which names July Indian-grass plumes a reconstruction error.

july.appearance: Fine emerald fountains; the fragrant panicle comes in late August.

july.appearance: Brilliant orange flat umbels on hairy stems — the loudest colour on the drier ground.

species.note: Dossier tags the scattered-forb row I/C and this is the dry-ground member of it: butterfly weed wants sand, and no source places it on the lake-plain prairie at the forks. Recorded conjectural, at the bottom of the density band, so a critic can see it is our guess.

note: Andreas documents the West Side as open prairie; that it carried a wet-mesic as well as a wet community follows from the lake-plain relief and the regional flora, not from any account of this site. The whole zone is an inference.
